title: La cuenta dividida en el café de Madrid

dialogue.speaker: Carmen
dialogue.spanish: Oye, Pablo, pues el camarero dice que no nos divide la cuenta aquí en la terraza.
dialogue.english: Hey, Pablo, well the waiter says he won't split the bill for us out here on the patio.

dialogue.speaker: Pablo
dialogue.spanish: ¡Qué fuerte, tía! Bueno, no pasa nada, pago yo todo con mi tarjeta porque sé que andas sin pasta.
dialogue.english: That's wild, girl! Well, no worries, I'll pay the whole thing with my card since I know you're out of cash.

slang.actualMeaning: out of money / broke (very common slang across Spain)
slang.example: No salgo este finde porque ando sin pasta.

dialogue.speaker: Carmen
dialogue.spanish: Mil gracias, tío. O sea, te hago un Bizum de doce euros ahora mismo por mis tostadas y el café cortado.
dialogue.english: Thanks a million, dude. I mean, I'll send you a 12-euro Bizum transfer right now for my toast and espresso.

slang.example: ¡Gracias por esperarme a la salida, tío!

dialogue.speaker: Pablo
dialogue.spanish: Tranqui, cuando puedas me lo pasas. Pero deja que pida el datáfono en la barra para no tardar.
dialogue.english: Relax, send it whenever you can. But let me ask for the card terminal at the bar so we don't take long.

dialogue.speaker: Carmen
dialogue.spanish: Sí, porfa, que encima se está levantando un frío de narices aquí afuera.
dialogue.english: Yes, please, especially since it's getting freezing cold out here.

dialogue.speaker: Pablo
dialogue.spanish: Vale, ya está pagado. Vámonos pitando que el último metro de la línea dos cierra en veinte minutos.
dialogue.english: Okay, it's paid. Let's get out of here fast because the last Line 2 metro closes in twenty minutes.

slang.actualMeaning: Let's leave in a big hurry / right away (irse pitando)
slang.example: Salí pitando de la oficina para no perder el tren.

questions.question: What problem do Carmen and Pablo run into at the Madrid café?
options: The waiter says he won't split the bill on the patio
The credit card terminal is broken
The kitchen ran out of toast and coffee
They forgot their phones at home
questions.explanation: Carmen says: 'el camarero dice que no nos divide la cuenta aquí en la terraza.'

questions.question: How does Carmen offer to pay Pablo back for her share?
options: She gives him a 20-euro bill in cash
She sends him a 12-euro Bizum mobile transfer
She buys his metro ticket at the station
She promises to buy breakfast tomorrow
questions.explanation: Carmen says: 'te hago un Bizum de doce euros ahora mismo por mis tostadas y el café cortado.'

questions.question: Why do they need to leave the café quickly at the end?
options: It is starting to rain on the patio
The last Line 2 metro closes in 20 minutes
They have a movie reservation at eight
The café is closing its terrace
questions.explanation: Pablo says: 'Vámonos pitando que el último metro de la línea dos cierra en veinte minutos.'

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: When Pablo says 'andas sin pasta' and 'vámonos pitando', what do 'pasta' and 'irse pitando' mean in Spain?
options: 'Pasta' = money/cash; 'irse pitando' = to leave in a hurry
'Pasta' = Italian food; 'irse pitando' = to whistle a song
'Pasta' = patience; 'irse pitando' = to take a taxi
'Pasta' = battery; 'irse pitando' = to argue with the waiter
questions.explanation: In Spain, 'pasta' is slang for money/cash, and 'irse pitando' means to leave in a rush!
